prompt:
High-quality anime footage. High-density 3D toon/cel-look. Cinematic high-fantasy action set in a rainy magic city. A pink-haired girl mage intercepts a giant black dragon's fire breath with a magic shield, teleports to the side using the counterforce, and fires a high-output beam from a convergence gate on her right palm, causing the dragon to crumble into black ash and magic particles.
[Character Identity and Role of Reference Images]
image1 is the top priority reference for the protagonist's face and identity. Maintain a soft oval young face, small chin, large blue-violet to purple-pink eyes, multi-layered iris with white highlights, delicate eye area, long coral pink twin-tails, light bangs, lavender flowers on both sides, and black-purple ribbons with gold decorations throughout.
image2 is the reference for the protagonist's outfit, decorations, full-body design, and equipment. Maintain a slender and small build, navy-to-purple gold-trimmed cape, white frill blouse, black-purple corset, purple multi-layered pleated skirt, white knee-highs, dark purple boots with metal fittings, waist belt, amethyst crystals, magic potions, and a magic book with gold decorations.
If references conflict, prioritize image1 for the face, eyes, and hair ornaments, and image2 for the outfit, build, and equipment. The two images are only for appearance; do not bring background, composition, poses, white background, or layout lines into the video.
Only allowed changes are focused expressions, eye direction, breathing, combat stance, and natural movement of hair/cape/skirt. Do not allow face averaging, feature mixing, outfit changes, equipment multiplication, or additional characters.
[Art Style: High-Density 3D Toon/Cel-Look]
This style does not override character identity. Fine, delicate colored outlines. Clear two-to-three-stage cel shading and transparent intermediate shadows on the face, hair, and outfit. Multi-layered highlights on eyes and hair. Use pink, lavender, navy, purple, and gold as the main color axis for the protagonist. Distinctly depict cloth, frills, leather, metal, amethyst, wet stone, and glass with different reflections. Theatrical-grade key animation, high-quality compositing, and dense background art. For magic, use high-brightness graphic VFX, volumetric light, additive emission, and directional motion blur. Avoid thick black outlines, flat single-layer shadows, or low-density plastic CG looks.
[Equipment and State Transitions]
Only one magic book. Maintain the same binding and thickness throughout. Open it with the left hand only in Cut 1, close it and return it to the waist holder in Cut 2. Keep amethyst crystals and potions attached to the belt. All attacks come from the right palm, not the book. Do not introduce new items not in image2.
[Black Dragon Fixing]
Only one giant black four-legged winged dragon, about four times the protagonist's height. One head, two horns, two glowing blue-white eyes, a continuous neck and torso, four legs with three claws each. One pair of wings continuous from the back bones. One tail branching from the lower back to the tip. The impact point is a single point on the chest scales. No extra heads, legs, or wings.
[Setting]
A massive magic city after the rain. Grand avenues of wet obsidian and blue-gray stone, shallow puddles, ancient cracks, and crumbling arch bridges. Surrounded by soaring magic towers, spires, floating turrets, and giant crystal pillars. City lighting is cyan, royal blue, violet, and purple. Keep background light one step darker than the protagonist to highlight her pink, lavender, and gold colors. No readable text; only abstract geometric patterns glowing faintly on stone and crystal surfaces.
[Space and Continuity]
Cuts 1-2: Protagonist in the left foreground, dragon in the right middle ground. Attack axis is a diagonal from back-right to front-left.
Cut 2: Teleportation through a magic gate momentarily swaps left-right positioning once.
Cuts 3-6: Protagonist in the right foreground, dragon in the left background. Align the right palm, gate center, beam, and dragon's chest in a straight line. Do not swap left-right positions after this.
In adjacent cuts, change at least two of the following: camera height, distance to protagonist, character size, or vanishing axis. Use camera movement to show contact, force, or space, not as a substitute for character movement. Maintain natural acceleration and parallax.
Cut 1: Fire Breath and Shield
Black dragon is in the right background. Steps into the stone floor, pulls neck back, chest swells, and throat glows orange-purple.
Protagonist is in the left foreground. Opens the magic book with the left hand and thrusts the right palm forward. Three layers of magic shields with white cores, cyan outer light, and purple-pink edges expand and counter-rotate at different speeds.
As the dragon swings its neck down, orange-purple fire breath travels straight from right-back to left-front, evaporating puddles. The fire splits around the shield and flows backwards. The impact causes the shield layers to flex and glow outward in a chain reaction.
The counterforce pushes back through the protagonist's palm, wrist, elbow, shoulder, and hips; her back foot scrapes the wet stone. Hair, flowers, cape, and skirt billow back with a time delay.
The camera moves from a low position along the fire axis towards the protagonist's rear-diagonal, keeping the shield, hands, profile, and dragon head in view.
Cut 2: Counterforce to Teleport
The protagonist pushes back the flexed front shield with her right palm, channeling the force into a right hip rotation. She closes the book with her left hand and returns it to the holder.
At the same moment, the pushed shield expands into a large arc that crosses the lens as a full-screen wipe.
When the arc clears, the protagonist appears on a crumbling arch bridge to the dragon's left. Show the landing through ground contact, knee compression, hip drop, and trailing cape/hair.
The dragon remains in its post-fire pose, beginning to turn its neck and eyes toward the new position.
The camera changes axis during the full-screen wipe, dropping from a high rear-diagonal to a lower three-quarter view.
Cut 3: Convergence Gate
Protagonist's chest-up close-up. From a diagonal front view, the camera turns gently about 15 degrees around the face

prompt:
写实暗黑特摄 | 昆虫仿生装甲美学 | 破损装甲 | 战损变形 | 荒野废墟

[人物与基础设定]
面部：上传图片参考图 1，100% 还原面部特征、脸型、发型。保留暗沉痕迹，可美化，但整体面部表情需冷峻。全程表情阴郁。变身时仅有轻微痛苦，眉间仅有轻微的川字纹，拒绝亢奋与眼神高光，保持压迫感。
服饰：参考图 1，无腰带结构。佩戴哑光金属异形装置手套。
场景：荒野废墟，微风，扬尘，阴沉荒地，灰蓝色天空。远处天空偶尔划过带火光的陨石碎片。

prompt:
Ultra-High Mobility/Non-Aerodynamic Autonomous Attack Aircraft vs. Humanoid High-Speed Combat Robot

[Video Concept] A giant high-speed combat robot commands approximately 10 fist-sized autonomous attack aircraft, evading machine gun fire from a giant humanoid combat robot through abnormal three-dimensional maneuvers that completely ignore the common sense of aircraft. The small attack aircraft do not turn; they move linearly at high speeds, stop suddenly, and instantaneously bend the movement vector itself at acute angles of 90, 120, or 150+ degrees to accelerate instantly in a different direction. They change positions to stereoscopically 'erode' the space around the enemy robot, deploying in multiple directions before the enemy can react. Finally, signaled by a large downward swing from the command robot, the 10 units synchronize perfectly for a simultaneous all-out attack from all directions. The enemy robot is engulfed in a massive explosion.

Overall Video Theme: "A swarm of autonomous attack aircraft that leap through space itself at high speed, rather than flying."

[World Setting] Far future. An era where three-dimensional maneuverable weapons, inexplicable by conventional aerodynamics, have been realized through advanced propulsion technology, omnidirectional attitude control, and artificial gravity control. The setting is over a massive futuristic city. A sea of clouds and giant cumulonimbus cover the spaces between massive skyscrapers, with explosions, smoke, and debris from combat in the distance. Daytime. Strong winds. High-altitude giant clouds. Aerial combat between giant humanoid high-speed robots. Next-generation aerial combat between a manned high-speed combat robot and a swarm of autonomous small attack aircraft. The small aircraft are not conventional aircraft; they do not rely on lift or turn radius but change movement vectors instantly via omnidirectional thrust. Their inertia appears extremely low. They stop instantly during high-speed movement and move in a different direction without deceleration. The movement looks like high-speed switching of spatial coordinates rather than "flight."

[Visual Style] Theatrical Japanese animation quality. Ultra-high-quality cel animation. Precise mecha animation. High-end sci-fi action. High-density drawing. High-definition cel shading. Realistic physics-based lighting. Sharp, precise line art. Complex mechanical details. Movie-quality compositing. Bold perspective. Great depth. High spatial density.

[Animation Direction] Most Important Motion Principles: Explosive animation, snappy timing, strong anticipation, powerful acceleration, large body mechanics, sharp ease-out, heavy follow-through, pronounced inertia, dynamic camera choreography, fast action arcs, high kinetic energy. Every movement begins decisively and ends with visible momentum. No sluggish movement. The movement of the large robot conveys massive mass. Clear anticipation before starting. The shoulders, waist, and legs move in coordination. Clear follow-through from weight during sudden stops. Shoulders, elbows, and wrists follow with a slight delay after arm swings. The entire frame drifts slightly due to inertia after high-speed movement. Conversely, small attack aircraft are the opposite of the large robot—extremely agile, small, fast, and precise. They start and stop in an instant. The time from start to maximum speed is extremely short. Eliminate wasteful preparatory movements. Agility, efficiency, and mechanically precise movement are prioritized. "Snappy movement," "instant change of position," and "movement the moment a decision is made" are the top priorities.

[Colors and Lighting] Command Robot: White, gunmetal, navy base with small red markings. Drones: Dark metallic, pale blue luminescent parts, pale blue propulsion light. Enemy Robot: Dark gray, black, navy heavy armor with red sensors. Sunlight is strong and harsh. Intense volumetric light from between clouds. Sharp highlights on armor. Explosions emphasize white, orange, and red.

[Large Command Robot] Height approx 8m. Slender, athlete-like humanoid silhouette. Long limbs, narrow waist, angular armor. Streamlined, aggressive head. Narrow luminescent sensors. White, gunmetal, navy armor. Small red markings. A launch unit on the back stores 10 drones. No large handheld weapons; hands are free, controlling drones via conductor-like gestures.

[Enemy High-Speed Combat Robot] Height approx 9m. Massive presence. Equipped with large propulsion units for high-speed flight. Maintains humanoid silhouette. Heavy armor. Built-in machine guns in arms. Fires massive rounds while flying. High firepower but cannot change direction instantly like drones; has clear inertia and needs to tilt for turns. Sudden stops cause the body to drift forward.

[Small Autonomous Attack Aircraft] Approx 10 units. Fist-sized. Angular mechanical structure. No wings or tail fins. Omnidirectional thrust units. Not small fighters, but autonomous spatial weapons. [Movement Principles] Do not turn like aircraft. No banking, no large arcs, no turn radius. Basic movement: Linear move -> Instant stop -> Acute angle turn -> Instant acceleration. Locus is straight lines and sharp angles. Instant vector changes (90/120/150 deg). Movements like spatial jumping.

[Camera Direction] Avoid fixed heights. Use low/high angles, bird's-eye, worm's-eye, horizontal, diagonal, close-ups, and telephoto compression. prompt: Task: Dreamina Seedance 2.5 — Omni ReferenceDuration: 30 secondsAspect ratio: 16:9Editorial target: 24fps, F000-F719 [Generation Goal]A high-speed combat battle involving only three characters: @Image1, @Image2, and @Image3. Develop offense and defense over 10 cuts. No weapons; use a combination of rushes, dodges, palm strikes, elbow strikes, kicks, throws, and aerial attacks. Do not fix the expressions of the three characters. Change them to alertness, surprise, irritation, concentration, provocation, exhilaration, and relief in response to the offense and defense. Express specifically through eyes, eyebrows, mouth, gaze, breathing, and head tilt. Return characters to a recognizable form only at moments of stopping, posing, contact, or landing. During high-speed movement, always break down the finished human body and replace it with a small number of liquid brushstrokes, rough watercolor planes, and short afterimages based on each character's color scheme. Do not simply add speed lines or motion blur to a finished figure. The flowing brushstrokes themselves are the character. [Material Roles]@Image1 = Character A. One and the same person. Uses yellow bob hair, cat ears, green eyes, light blue and white clothes, yellow trim, triangular tie decoration, pink backpack, pink boots, light blue tail with a yellow triangular tip as identifying information. @Image2 = Character B. One and the same person. Uses a yellow-green round bob, two leaf-like ears, golden eyes, white puff sleeves, pink bowtie, dark green shorts with suspenders, green boots, a long yellow-green tuft continuing from the back of the head with a round tip as identifying information. @Image3 = Character C. One and the same person. Uses vivid blue long hair and ponytail, two white horns, pointed ears, golden eyes, star-shaped earrings, dark red Japanese-style clothing, black skirt, black belt and back ribbon, black knee-highs, and red geta as identifying information. Do not treat three-view diagrams as clones. Do not swap the faces, hair, costumes, color schemes, ears, horns, tails, back hair, or decorations of the three. However, the expressions in the reference images are not fixed and should change according to the battle situation. Do not use white backgrounds or explanatory text. Do not generate weapons. Do not use the backpack, tail, back hair, horns, or geta as detached weapons. [Environment]A giant festival square based on a white paper surface. A giant vermilion pillar and watercolor stalls on the left, a sequence of vermilion torii gates in the center back, a red lantern shelf on the right, and light blue cubes and firework-like brushstrokes in the sky. Draw the background with translucent watercolors, broken ink lines, pencil composition lines, and wide white margins. Do not enclose the floor, pillars, torii, stalls, or lanterns with closed outlines. The background lines also tremble slightly, changing in density and position, but the amount of variation is weaker than that of the characters. Maintain the background layout in all cuts. Do not include combatants, crowds, or additional characters other than the three. [Unstable Line Rule]Draw the entire video with 'continuously generated lines and watercolors.' Do not clean up each frame from the previous one; redraw each frame as a new rough sketch. Do not create a single outline surrounding the person. Do not enclose the head, shoulders, arms, torso, or legs with continuous lines; always leave 30-60% of the body's outer circumference as white gaps in the paper. Recognize the character's form intermittently through short, broken pencil lines, irregular watercolor boundaries, dry brush marks, eraser marks, and doubled redraw lines. Do not maintain the same line in the same position for more than 3 frames. Lines change in position, thickness, density, length, pressure, and curvature every frame. They break in the middle, split into two, and parts disappear. Do not use a single uniform line width for the whole body. Do not keep line density constant. Irregularly alternate frames with extremely few lines, frames with dense redraw lines, and frames where most of the outer circumference disappears. Do not create a finished outer circumference for the face either. Do not draw both eyes, nose, mouth, jaw, and cheeks clearly at the same time. Leave only the minimum lines to read the expression, such as the outer side of one eye disappearing, the mouth cutting off midway, eyebrows becoming double, or cheek lines melting into watercolor. Do not fit the watercolor accurately inside the lines. Create bleeding, protrusion, white unpainted areas, uneven shading, and misregistration. [Line and Color Delay]Body movement takes the lead, pencil lines follow about 1-2 frames late, and watercolor color planes follow about another 1-2 frames late. Late lines and color planes do not completely overlap the body and remain as short afterimages torn in the direction of movement. Afterimages are not copies of the finished person but brushstrokes and color planes that indicate only the direction of the arms, legs, hair, tail, and costume. Even when stopped, do not return the lines to a clean-up state. The person's face, clothing, and posture become legible, but the gaps in the outer circumference, double lines, watercolor bleeding, and misregistration are maintained. [Mandatory Motion Deformation]Draw only about 60% of the human body for weak actions. Draw only about 30-40% for medium-speed actions. Draw only about 10-20% for high-speed actions. At maximum speed, represent the character with only 3-5 brushstrokes and 2-3 rough color planes. Character A high-speed action = yellow, light blue, white, and pink brushstroke group. Character B high-speed action = yellow-green, dark green, white, and a small amount of pink brushstroke group. Character C high-speed action = blue, dark red, black, and a small amount of golden brushstroke group. During high-speed action, do not connect the head, torso, arms, and legs with a correct human structure. Turn arms into long liquid brushstrokes, kicking legs into extremely elongated color planes, and rotating torsos into crushed arcs, triangles, or twisted watercolor surfaces. Temporarily disconnect limbs during jumps. Compress the torso in the direction of travel during sudden stops. Shift the hips and shoulders in different directions during turns. [Expression Direction]Character A: Starts with alertness, changes to a proud smile upon successful evasion, surprise when an attack is diverted, playful provocation during a melee, strong concentration in the late stages, and finally a satisfied, breathless smile. Character B: Starts with cautious observation, sharp concentration when interrupting, momentary surprise when an attack is dodged, a competitive smile during aerial attacks, a desperate expression in the final stages, and finally a soft, relieved expression. Character C: Starts with calm confidence, smiles slightly after dodging the first attack, furrows eyebrows during a pincer attack, sharp concentration while counterattacking, an exhilarated smile during the three-way melee, and finally a provocative one-sided smile. Do not finish the face during high-speed action. Indicate emotions with a single stroke of the eye, the tilt of an eyebrow, a short line of the mouth, or the direction of head brushstrokes. Make expressions legible only at moments when speed drops. [Cut 1 | 0.0-2.5s | F000-F059 | Triangular Confrontation]Initial state: Fixed wide. Character A is in the left foreground, Character B is in the right foreground, and Character C is in the center back. They form a triangle with each other in sight. Primary event: Show the appearance and positions of the three from F000-F023. A narrows eyes and is wary of C, B looks back and forth between A and C and breathes cautiously. C raises their chin slightly and shows composure with a one-sided smirk. From F024-F041, A lowers their hips, B opens half a step to the side, and C slides their geta to lower their center of gravity. From F042-F059, the three step out simultaneously. End state: The travel directions of the three converge in the center. The expressions and body circumferences are legible, but the lines are not closed and are redrawn every frame. [Cut 2 | 2.5-5.0s | F060-F119 | A vs C First Strike]Initial state: Low angle near the ground. A on the left, C in the center, B in the right back. Primary event: From F060-F075, A breaks down into yellow, light blue, and pink brushstrokes and rushes low from left to right. From F076-F087, A connects a leg sweep to a spinning kick. C breaks down into blue, dark red, and black brushstrokes, rotates, and evades the kick by a hair's breadth. Only just before contact from F088-F095 do A's eyes open wide and C smiles slightly. Do not draw the whole face, show only through fragments of eyes, eyebrows, and mouth. From F096-F119, A passes by C and slides to the right, leaving fragments of a surprised face. End state: A is in the right foreground, C is in the center, B is in the right back. C's composure increases, and A refocuses their expression. [Cut 3 | 5.0-8.0s | F120-F191 | B's Interruption]Initial state: Medium wide horizontal position. C in the center, A on the right, B in the right back. Primary event: From F120-F137, B lowers their eyebrows, breaks down into yellow-green and dark green brushstrokes, and enters from right to left. From F138-F153, B performs a spinning leg sweep passing under both of their feet. From F154-F167, A jumps vertically, and their legs and tail stretch into watercolor bands. The moment the evasion is successful, the corners of A's eyes droop and a smirk forms provocatively. C sinks low, folding their body to dodge B's kick. From F168-F179, B's eyes open wide for a moment, showing surprise at being dodged. From F180-F191, B furrows their eyebrows and concentrates on the next attack while sliding left. End state: B lands on the left, C in the center, and A in the center back. [Cut 4 | 8.0-11.0s | F192-F263 | C's Continuous Counterattack]Initial state: Low diagonal composition. B on the left, C in the center, A in the back. Primary event: From F192-F207, C's smile disappears and eyebrows drop sharply. C breaks down into 3-5 blue, dark red, and black brushstrokes and accelerates rapidly from left to right. From F208-F223, C performs a palm strike on B, an elbow strike on A, and a spinning back kick in one continuous motion. During the attack, C does not return to a finished body. Only a single golden stroke for the eye and a concentrated eyebrow line appear within the brushstroke group. From F224-F239, B evades backwards as a green arc, and A escapes sideways by splitting into short yellow and pink lines. From F240-F251, the arms and legs of the three cross for just a moment. A opens their mouth briefly in surprise, and B grits their teeth. From F252-F263, C passes to the right side and shows an exhilarated one-sided smile. End state: C is on the right, B on the left, A in the center back. All three are standing. [Cut 5 | 11.0-14.5s | F264-F347 | A and B Pincer Attack]Initial state: High diagonal overhead view. C on the right, A in the center back, B on the left. Primary event: From F264-F283, A and B exchange a short look. A shows a confident smile, B shows a focused face with lowered eyebrows. The two run towards C simultaneously; A performs a low flying kick and B performs a spinning kick. From F284-F303, C furrows their eyebrows and changes their body into thin blue, red, and black lines to slip through the gap between the two kicks. From F304-F323, A and B open their eyes wide just before colliding with each other, tuck their legs, and change direction in mid-air. From F324-F347, the three move apart in a circle. C gives a small smile for breaking the pincer attack, A furrows their eyebrows regretfully, and B exhales and gauges the next distance. End state: B on the left, C in the center, A on the right. [Cut 6 | 14.5-18.0s | F348-F431 | Sequence of Grabs and Throws]Initial state: Circling tracking shot. B on the left, C in the center, A on the right. Primary event: From F348-F367, A smiles provocatively and tries to jump onto C's shoulder. C changes to a focused, almost expressionless face, catches A's wrist to change their direction of motion, and throws them low. Make only the contact point briefly legible. From F368-F387, A becomes a group of yellow and pink brushstrokes and falls while rotating. Surprised eyes and an open mouth appear for a moment, then immediately break down into lines. From F388-F407, B throws a heel kick at C while passing in mid-air. B narrows their eyes and shows a competitive smile. From F408-F419, C catches it with their forearm and flows B's leg line outward. C's eyebrows rise slightly, showing surprise at the unexpected strength. From F420-F431, A regains posture just above the floor, clenches their mouth regretfully, and performs a three-point landing. End state: A is in the right foreground, B is in the left foreground, and C is in the center back. [Cut 7 | 18.0-21.5s | F432-F515 | 3D Offense and Defense Using the Background]Initial state: Wide shot showing the left vermilion pillar, center torii, and right lantern shelf simultaneously. Primary event: From F432-F451, B runs to the left pillar. Their expression changes to an exhilarated smile, and they step on the pillar once to bounce off diagonally. From F452-F471, A jumps to the right stall roof, kicks the roof, and reverses to the center. A shakes off the regret and narrows their eyes joyfully. From F472-F491, C anticipates the trajectories of the two and stays out of both attack lines with a low rotation while keeping a sharp gaze. During the high-speed section, the three become brushstroke groups with their own independent color schemes. From F492-F503, only the lanterns and stall cloths shake from the wind pressure. prompt: [00:00–00:02] Wide establishing shot of the bizarre fantasy forest @image3 . Towering flesh-like tree trunks packed with blinking embedded eyes rise on both sides, glowing blue liquid runs down roots into occult circular markings on the ground, red storm sky beyond. The corridor feels alive and watching. CAM: slow low push forward, ominous and quiet. [00:02–00:04] The girl @image1 runs into frame through the center path, sprinting hard toward camera, red coat flaring, glowing eyes wide with fear and focus. Her shoes splash through glowing blue runoff, hair bouncing violently. CAM: handheld-style backward chase shot, low and fast. [00:04–00:06] Whip-pan reveal behind her: multiple grotesque monsters @image2 skitter and bound into the corridor, drooling blue slime, eyes rolling wildly, teeth bared. They move with jerky inhuman speed, legs scraping over the slick ground. CAM: snap whip-pan, then brief forward rush with the pack. [00:06–00:08] Sakuga cut barrage: close-up of her @image1 pounding feet through glowing symbols; coat sleeve whipping past lens; monster claws stabbing into the wet soil; embedded eyes in the trees blinking open; blue fluid splashing; one monster lunges just short of her back. Fast, sharp, chaotic cuts. [00:08–00:10] @image1 cuts hard left around a root mass, nearly slipping, catches herself, then vaults over a stream of glowing liquid. One monster @image2 crashes into the roots and another leaps across the frame with jaws wide. CAM: side tracking shot matching her sprint, aggressive parallax through the living trunks. [00:10–00:12] @image1 reaches a circular sigil clearing and skids to a stop at center. The monsters @image2 spread out around her at the edge of the frame, surrounding but not yet striking. The forest eyes all seem to stare inward. CAM: overhead-descending angle into a dramatic low angle on her bracing herself. [00:12–00:14] Horror standoff beat. @image1 slowly raises her head, glowing eyes intensifying, red coat settling in the blue-lit air. The nearest monster @image2 creeps forward, drool stretching, others twitching in anticipation. Blue runoff pulses brighter through the ground symbols. CAM: slow push-in, trembling atmosphere. [00:14–00:15] Final impact image: one monster @image2 explodes forward into frame as @image1 snaps into motion to counter, freezing on the instant before collision—glowing eyes, claws, teeth, flaring coat, occult light reflecting across the flesh-trees. Hard cut ending.

[00:08–00:10] 她 @image1 猛地向左绕过一团树根，差点滑倒，随即稳住身形，然后跃过一道发光的液体。一只怪物 @image2 撞上树根，另一只则张着大嘴跃过画面。镜头：侧向跟踪镜头，配合她的冲刺，通过活体树干展现出强烈的视差效果。

title_en: Candid Late-Night Pizza Moment with Handheld Camcorder Aesthetic
changes: 仅做提取与空白/Markdown 代码块格式规范化，提示词文字未做任何改动（含错别字）；未收录任何图片/视频。
path: prompts/真人/现实向/生活与vlog/youmind-893--手持摄像机美学下的深夜披萨坦诚时刻.md
prompt:
A dim bedroom lit by a harsh on-camera flash. White bedsheets fill most of the frame, slightly wrinkled and textured. An open pizza box sits nearby on the bed, its lid tilted back, revealing a partially eaten pizza.

A young woman lies on her back across the bed, head tilted slightly toward the camera. She wears a playful shirt patterned with cartoon pizza slices. Her hair spreads across the pillow.

The camera is held very close above her with a wide consumer lens, creating slight perspective distortion. The flash flattens shadows and creates glossy highlights on her eyes and the pizza grease.

She lifts a slice of pepperoni pizza above her face.

Slowly, she lowers it toward her mouth.

The cheese stretches slightly from the slice as it moves. Oil glistens on the pepperoni under the flash. The slice bends naturally as gravity pulls the tip downward.

She takes a bite.

The crust compresses between her fingers. The cheese pulls and separates unevenly as she bites through it. A small strand of melted cheese briefly stretches before snapping.

Her eyes remain fixed toward the camera as she chews.

The camera remains very close and handheld, shifting slightly as if the person filming adjusts their grip. The flash creates harsh reflections across the pizza box and glossy toppings.

Image quality shows consumer analog artifacts: visible grain, slight color noise in darker areas, mild softness, and faint exposure fluctuation.

The camera lingers as she continues eating casually, the pizza slice slowly disappearing bite by bite.

Overall feeling: intimate, playful, and candid — a messy late-night pizza moment captured with a handheld camcorder in a pre-digital bedroom setting.

variants.label: YouMind 提供的中文版本（README_zh.md）
variants.text:
一间昏暗的卧室，被刺眼的机载闪光灯照亮。白色床单占据了画面大部分，略有褶皱和纹理。一个打开的披萨盒放在床边，盒盖向后倾斜，露出一个吃了一半的披萨。

一个年轻女子仰卧在床上，头微微倾向镜头。她穿着一件印有卡通披萨图案的俏皮衬衫。头发散落在枕头上。

镜头在她上方非常近的距离拍摄，使用广角消费级镜头，造成轻微的透视畸变。闪光灯使阴影变平，并在她的眼睛和披萨油渍上 tạo 出光泽高光。

她将一片意大利辣香肠披萨举到脸上方。

她慢慢地将其放到嘴边。

披萨片移动时，奶酪略微拉伸。闪光灯下，意大利辣香肠上的油光闪闪。披萨片在重力作用下自然弯曲，尖端向下垂。

她咬了一口。

饼皮在她的指间被压扁。她咬下去时，奶酪不均匀地拉扯和分离。一小缕融化的奶酪短暂地拉伸后断裂。

她咀嚼时，眼睛一直盯着镜头。

镜头保持非常近的距离，手持拍摄，轻微晃动，仿佛拍摄者正在调整握持姿势。闪光灯在披萨盒和光泽的配料上 tạo 出刺眼的反光。

图像质量显示出消费级模拟伪影：可见的颗粒感、较暗区域轻微的色彩噪点、轻微的柔和度以及微弱的曝光波动。

镜头在她继续随意进食时停留，披萨片一口一口地慢慢消失。

整体感觉：亲密、俏皮、真实——一个凌乱的深夜披萨时刻，在数码时代之前的卧室环境中，用手持摄像机捕捉。

prompt: Format: 16:9 | Look: Photorealistic, 8K, 35mm film, cool-toned night grade, shallow depth of field, lens grain, cinematic hard cuts, dynamic camera per shot CHARACTER DESCRIPTION The Woman (pre-transformation): Mid-20s, Western/European features, strikingly attractive and beautiful. Slim, toned, elegant build, roughly 5'8". Wardrobe: a fitted black leather jacket over a simple fitted top, dark high-waisted jeans, ankle boots — modern, stylish, urban-night aesthetic. Minimal jewelry (thin gold necklace) that will later echo the beast's gold markings. The Beast (post-transformation): Tall, lean, unmistakably feminine — never bulky or male-coded, and not wolf-like. Slender long-limbed frame, long legs ending in black-clawed paws. Thick ruff of cream-white fur across the chest. Coat mottled black, gold and cream. Crown of tall branching gold horns. Fine gold facial markings tracing her cheekbones and brow (echoing the woman's features). Amber-gold slit-pupil eyes. Long membranous black-and-gold wings. Trailing golden tendrils drifting from the horns and spine. The transformation is progressive and layered — skin to hide, fur in a traveling wave, muscle lengthening, nails to claws, horns branching, wings unfurling — surface-level morphing only, no wounds, no tearing, no blood. SETTING A generic Shibuya-style crossing at night — no real landmarks, brands, or logos; invented signage text only. Neon in magenta, cyan and violet, wet asphalt mirroring the light, drifting steam, light rain haze. A huge blood-red moon dominates the sky above the skyline throughout. PART 1 — 0:00–0:15 — "THE OMEN AND THE COLLAPSE" Shot 1 (0–4s) — The Red Moon Opens tight on the enormous blood-red moon above the skyline. Long continuous extreme crane-down past glowing tower screens (invented neon kanji-style signage) toward the crowded crossing below, then pushes through the crowd to settle on the woman walking among them, one hand pressed to her temple, head down, unsteady, hair damp with mist. Shot 2 (4–7s) — First Tremor Hard cut to a low tracking shot at hip height following her boots across wet asphalt — reflections of neon rippling with each step — as her stride breaks rhythm and she catches herself against an invisible wave of dizziness. Shot 3 (7–11s) — The Collapse Cut to handheld medium pushing with her through the crowd. She stumbles, breath shallow, face pale under the neon wash. Her knees buckle and she drops to the pavement. Shot 4 (11–15s) — The Empty Ring Wide crane shot as the crowd scatters back in a widening ring, phones raised, murmurs rippling outward, until she is alone, kneeling, at the dead center of the empty crossing — rain haze drifting through the neon light around her. PART 2 — 0:15–0:30 — "THE TRANSFORMATION" Shot 5 (15–26s) — One Unbroken Take Extreme low angle at asphalt level, 24mm wide lens, only her right hand in frame, pressed flat on the wet asphalt, oversized by wide-lens perspective. Camera zooms hard on the back of her hand: pale skin darkens into hide, cream-white and mottled gold-black fur emerges strand by strand, fingers lengthen, nails darken into black claws that gouge the asphalt. Camera tracks and pushes along the forearm following the wave of fur, rises to the shoulder, swings around to find her face in tight close-up — still human, jaw clenched, terror in her hazel-green eyes — then pushes into an extreme close-up of her eyes as the irises flood amber-gold, pupils narrowing to slits, the last trace of the woman vanishing. Camera pulls back into a fast orbiting handheld shake as the white ruff floods her chest, gold markings spread across her face, golden horns branch from her temples, wings unfurl behind her. The orbit whips to the front as the fully formed beast rises to full height. Shot 6 (26–30s) — The Roar Low, wide-angle hold as she plants her clawed paws and throws her head back — a full-body roar, wings snapping open to full span, golden tendrils whipping outward, neon light rippling across her mottled coat. PART 3 — 0:30–0:45 — "PANIC, PURSUIT AND THE HOWL" Shot 7 (30–33s) — Panic Fast handheld at street level as the beast sweeps her clawed limbs and lunges forward, wings flaring wide. The crowd breaks and scatters, people sprinting past the lens, camera whip-panning through the chaos as neon streaks smear across the wet asphalt. Shot 8 (33–36s) — The Chase Beat Low tracking shot alongside her as she bounds on all fours between stalled cars and scattering crowds, claws sparking faintly off metal and asphalt, wings half-folded for speed, camera struggling to keep pace — motion blur and lens flare from passing neon signs. Shot 9 (36–39s) — The Climb Fast upward-tracking shot as she launches from the crossing and scales a building face in fluid bounds, claws punching into the facade, mottled coat and white ruff catching the neon, wings half-folded. Camera rises with her, orbiting outward to reveal the city sprawling below. Shot 10 (39–42s) — The Perch Cut to a slow dolly-in on the rooftop ledge as she lands in a low crouch, wings settling against her back, chest heaving, gold facial markings glowing faintly under the moon, ears (horn-crown) tracking the city sounds below. Shot 11 (42–45s) — The Howl Low-angle wide on the rooftop tower — she stands tall, lit by neon from below, the enormous red moon directly behind her, her crown of golden horns and outstretched wings rim-lit against it. She rears back and howls, fur and golden tendrils rippling in the wind. Camera cranes slowly up and back into a vast wide, city lights sprawling out, rain drifting across the frame as the shot holds on the silhouette-and-glow composition for the final beat. EXTRA ACTION BEATS (optional inserts to extend further / alternate cuts) Insert after Shot 4: a tight cutaway of a dropped phone on wet asphalt, screen cracked, still recording, neon reflected in the cracked glass. Insert after Shot 6: a low static shot of scattered crowd members frozen mid-flight, silhouetted against a neon billboard, as the beast's shadow sweeps over them. Insert after Shot 9: a brief aerial drone-style shot circling the tower as steam vents hiss below her perch, city traffic streaking far beneath. Alternate ending extension: slow-motion feather/fur wisp caught in the wind drifting past camera as the howl fades, rain intensifying, screen fading to the red moon.

prompt:
Photorealistic live-action video, shot on cinema camera, natural skin texture, realistic lighting, 16:9 horizontal.

Setting: A cozy indoor room with warm ambient lighting, posters on wall, hanging lamp, modern furniture.

Subject: A young blonde American woman with shoulder-length golden blonde hair, fair skin, wearing a gray hooded jacket. She faces the camera from waist up.

The video has TWO distinct phases — do NOT repeat the same motion throughout.

=== FIRST HALF (seconds 0–5): Horizontal spring stretch ===
- Both hands at face height. Thumb and index finger on each hand form L-shaped viewfinder corners facing inward.
- Purely horizontal motion: hands close together in front of her face, then pull outward left and right to shoulder width, then pull back to center. Repeat this lateral spring cycle 2–3 times.
- Smooth, elastic sideways pull. Forearms stay level. Elbows move outward as hands spread.

=== SECOND HALF (seconds 5–10): Varied finger-frame gestures ===
- Transition naturally into different finger-frame poses. She rotates and flips her wrists so the thumb-index frame orientation changes.
- Always keep thumb and index finger extended upright forming the corner of a viewfinder on BOTH hands.
- End with hands at a relaxed wide finger-frame pose.

NOT animated, NOT cartoon, NOT 3D render, NOT anime — real filmed footage. Stable camera, no zoom, no cuts.

path: prompts/真人/特效向/古装仙侠玄幻/youmind-8984--Cinematic-Wuxia-Suspense-Scene-Prompt.md
prompt:
核心风格
电影级写实质感，采用参考图驱动的活世界设计。整体从古典武侠悬疑自然过渡到克制情境喜剧，强调宏大中国山水尺度、可触摸的天气、自然体积空气、细腻胶片颗粒，以及由环境自身因果关系推动剧情。
环境规划

正式构图前，先执行一轮无声环境规划。
全部参考图共同决定：

地形逻辑
建筑语言

空间尺度

材质年代

植被生态
水系走向

天气状态
云层结构
雾气规律
主光方向
整体色彩
反光表面
空气纵深
将这些信息重组为一个全新、统一、物理自洽、此前未出现过的景观。
环境必须持续活着：
瀑布和水渠始终流动
山雾顺地势游走
植被服从统一风向
云层阴影在湿石上缓慢移动
倒影持续变化

远处建筑在雾中时隐时现
前中后景始终具备真实视差

角色锁定
角色 A
同一个来自 @图片1 的 25–30 岁东亚剑仙女子。
同一张脸，黑色长发，白色刺绣真丝汉服，玉石饰品，纤细身材比例，白色布靴，银色长剑。
角色 B
同一个来自 @图片2 的 20–25 岁东亚小师妹。
同一张脸，黑色编发，青绿色汉服，娇小身材比例，深色布鞋，深色长剑。
硬约束：
身份稳定
面部稳定
服装稳定

长剑连续性稳定
全程只出现两名可见角色

分镜

镜头 1｜0–5s
全景或远景。
两人从鞋到头完整站在一条雨后湿润的悬崖古道上，下方是层叠梯田与轰鸣峡谷。

画面内持续存在：

瀑布灌入山间水渠
竹林随风以不同幅度弯曲
山雾沿低洼地势流动
湿润石面反射移动云层的光
远处瓦顶建筑在雾中若隐若现
峡谷深处突然传来巨大而规律的“咚——咚——”声，像军阵战鼓。
两人瞬间同时转头锁定声音方向。
镜头 2｜5–10s

中景或牛仔景。
保持同样两名女子、同样地理结构、同样服装和道具。
两人谨慎沿石路向下移动。
每一次“咚”声都引发真实环境反馈：

路边积水产生震纹

落叶轻跳
悬挂木牌轻颤
桥索细微共振
摄影机横向跟拍，并从近景竹叶之间穿过，用自然视差揭示新的空间纵深，同时保持世界布局不变。
对白：

白衣剑仙低声说：“有人擂鼓。”
小师妹拔出长剑，屏息倾听

镜头 3｜10–15s

特写或极近特写揭示。
摄影机穿过最后一层山雾，揭露真正声源：
同一条瀑布推动一座巨大的古代木制水轮。
水轮通过木制连杆规律抬起三根巨大的舂米木杵，依次砸入石臼，在梯田旁发出与先前完全相同的震耳“战鼓声”。

现场并无敌人。
对白：

小师妹缓慢放低长剑，愣着说：“师姐…… 他们在舂米。”
白衣剑仙仍极其严肃地观察水轮，平静回答：“粮草如此充足，确实难打。”
停留在两人一本正经的表情上，最后再落下一记巨大的舂米“咚——”作为收尾。
技术规格

严格总时长 15 秒

16:9 横屏

三个连续清晰镜头
原生同步普通话对白与环境声音
人物身份、地理关系、道具全程稳定

保持真实自然视差
水流、山雾、植被、倒影和水轮机械始终持续运动

木材、石材、真丝衣料和水雾飞溅符合统一物理逻辑
不生成字幕

始终只出现两名可见角色

Seedance Video Prompt | 15 Seconds | Sword Training Correction
I. Generation Goal
Movie-grade realistic texture, pure ancient Chinese Xianxia aesthetics.
Overall features:
Elegant and clear martial arts choreography
Restrained relationship-based comedy
Arri Alexa film camera texture
Clear and stable facial details
Natural morning volumetric light
Fine film grain
Core Reversal Principle
The plot is entirely driven by the characters' own personalities, goals, and interactions. The environment is just an independent, real, and living world; it must not trigger the plot, solve problems, change character goals, or comment on the plot.
II. Environment Generation Principles
Before formal composition, all reference images jointly determine the environment's DNA.
Co-evolve compatible features: Terrain, Architecture, Spatial Scale, Age of materials, Vegetation, Water systems, Weather, Clouds, Fog density, Lighting direction, Reflection relationships, Color systems, Atmospheric depth.
Then reorganize this information into a unique, complete, and logical new space.
Environment Requirements
Background movement must be continuous, natural, and physically accurate. The environment must be 'alive' but remain neutral in narration. The environment must not steal the spotlight or actively create gags or drive character relationships.
III. Scene Setting
Location: A stone sword-training platform at a mountain gate reorganized from all reference images.
Environmental Anchors: Moist stone slabs after rain, carved stone railings, ancient pines, bamboo forest, distant tiled-roof halls, a continuous flowing narrow water channel, layered distant mountains, slowly moving valley fog. These elements establish a clear, stable, and real spatial relationship.
IV. Character Settings
Character ID A | Senior Sister Sword Immortal
Strictly maintain the same identity as @Image 1.
25–30 year old East Asian female, oval face, fair natural skin tone, dark almond eyes, long black hair half-tied with a white jade hairpin. Tall and slender, wearing white cloth boots, white embroidered silk Hanfu with semi-transparent layered wide sleeves, silver waist seal, and a jade pendant. Holds a unique silver longsword.
Character ID B | Junior Sister
Strictly maintain the same identity as @Image 2.
20–25 year old East Asian female, rounded and lively face, black hair in braids, petite build. Wearing blue-green linen Hanfu, dark belt, wooden hairpin, and black cloth shoes. Holds a unique dark steel sword.
V. Lens Structure
Shot 1 | 0–5s | Wide or Long Shot
Establish the entire sword-training platform space. Both characters enter the frame completely from feet to head, formally bow with swords, then raise swords simultaneously.
Dialogue
Junior sister says seriously: 'No letting me win today.'
Camera and Environment Requirements
The frame first clearly establishes the spatial relationship of the platform. The two characters are the main focus. The water channel flows continuously, valley fog moves slowly, pine branches and bamboo sway at different magnitudes in the wind. Reflections on the wet stone surface exist naturally. These changes are for spatial realism only and do not participate in the plot.
Shot 2 | 5–10s | Medium or Cowboy Shot
Enter the sparring process. Junior sister launches a serious and clean frontal thrust.
Action Design
Junior sister completes a clear frontal thrust. Senior sister takes only one side step and blocks once. After blocking, she naturally holds the junior's sword wrist and gently adjusts the angle downward. Senior sister says: 'Wrist is high again.' Junior sister immediately pulls away, attacks again, senior sister blocks again while gently tapping the junior's front foot with her white boot to narrow her stance. Senior sister adds: 'Feet too wide.'
Environment Requirements
The same training platform remains stable. The water channel, fog, and vegetation continue their natural movements. Reflections change naturally with the camera angle. Background changes must remain neutral.
Shot 3 | 10–15s | Close-up or Extreme Close-up
Junior sister suddenly stops, her sword still in an offensive posture. She finally can't help asking.
Dialogue and Action
Junior sister asks: 'Sister, are you here for a duel or to teach me?'
Senior sister remains expressionless, only uses two fingers to gently push the junior's slightly tilted sword tip straight. Senior sister answers calmly: 'Win over your bad habits first.'
Complete pause for half a beat. Then: Junior sister glares at her but doesn't argue, instead silently adjusts her wrist angle and foot position as instructed. Then she strikes again.
Ending
Extreme close-up captures a very slight, almost imperceptible satisfied smile at the corner of the senior sister's mouth. The two longswords touch precisely off-screen with a single crisp metallic 'Clang' to end.
VI. Technical Requirements
Strict total duration: 15 seconds. 16:9 horizontal screen. Three continuous clear shots. Native synchronized Mandarin dialogue. No subtitles generated.
VII. Stability Requirements
Must strictly ensure: facial stability, clothing stability, sword stability, clear geographic relationships, clear spatial axes, logical actions, real body mechanics, and clean, restrained, readable martial arts movements.
VIII. Physical and Environmental Requirements
Elements like body movements, silk fabric, hair, water flow, mountain fog, vegetation, reflections, and spatial ambient sound must be real and natural. Only the two visible characters should appear.

Video Generation: Style] Vertical screen real-life pet funny short video, realistic home restaurant texture, soft natural sunlight, fixed mobile phone camera, slight handheld feel; anthropomorphic performance but the cat's body proportions, walking, fur, lighting, and mouth shape are realistic and high-quality. No subtitles, no text, no watermark, no clipping.

[Scene] Bright modern home restaurant. Light wood dining table in the bottom half, white porcelain rice bowls, chopsticks, and white plates with beef and side dishes on the table; a light-colored child's high chair in the background. Lens shot at eye level from across the table, the first half showing the cat in the high chair, the second half showing the cat approaching the camera from the side.
[Character] A real cat; only this cat appears in the whole film. It can anthropomorphically hold chopsticks with front paws, make aggrieved and coquettish reactions, but is still a four-legged real cat, not standing like a human, and no human hands appear. The cat's mouth must be strictly synchronized with the native Chinese audio. The cat's voice imitates a cute child's voice, and the owner is an adult female voice.
[00:00-00:02] Shot 1: Testing on the high chair. Fixed medium close-up. Cat sits in the high chair, bowls and chopsticks on the table; one front paw lightly touches the chopsticks, eyes looking at the camera seriously, tone showing expectation and testing, mouth naturally synced. Lip-sync: [00:00.15-00:01.03] 'Do you love me?' [00:01.07-00:01.83] Female voiceover: 'I don't love you anymore.'
[00:02-00:04.2] Shot 2: Leaving in anger. Maintain the original camera position. Cat frowns, ears slightly back, dissatisfied look, lets go of chopsticks, talks back while jumping from high chair to floor and walking away; jumping and landing must follow real cat movement. Lip-sync: [00:02.07-00:04.19] Cat huffs, speaking fast: 'If you don't love me, I don't love you either.'
[00:04.2-00:06.5] Shot 3: Crying and coquettishly trying to redeem. Short pause. Cat walks to the front side of the table and suddenly looks back at the camera, anger turning into grievance: eyes moist, brows drooping, mouth down, nose twitching. Not exaggerated wailing, but cute crying voice, anxious to reconcile; one front paw slightly raised as if trying to keep the person behind the camera. Lip-sync: [00:04.95-00:06.47] Voiceover, urgently: 'I love you, I love you, come back quick.'
[00:06.5-00:10] Shot 4: Crying and approaching, proudly agreeing. Cat continues running towards the lens from the side of the table, eyes still tearful, with slight aggrieved sobs while walking; cat's face gradually grows larger, filling the frame in close-up. Lip-sync: [00:08.03-00:08.27] Cat responds softly with a nasal sound: 'Mhm.' (crying tone) [00:08.27-00:10.00] Stops talking, cat looks straight at the camera aggrievedly, preserving the quiet pause at the end of the audio, natural ending, 9:16, 10s

The mountain gate corridor stone platform on a morning after rain. The same white-clad swordmaster senior sister and the same green-clad junior sister are located on both sides of the stone table.

[5–10s | Cowboy shot within a shot]

The same green-clad junior sister slowly reaches out to take the same bamboo scroll, while her other hand naturally rests by her sword.

The same white-clad senior sister maintains a completely calm expression and adds a sentence:

'I have already graded it for you.'

Nearby leaves naturally drift past the screen, forming realistic foreground parallax; the canal continues to flow, and mountain mist slowly wanders between the corridors.

The background always maintains only a sense of world presence and does not actively create new plot events.

The junior sister starts to unfold the bamboo scroll after taking it, maintaining continuous action for the next shot.

[10–15s | Close-up to extreme close-up]

The same bamboo scroll is fully unfolded.

Inside is not a secret manual, but an old love poem written by the same green-clad junior sister three years ago; the paper is densely written with neat, elegant red annotations.

The same green-clad junior sister freezes instantly and asks in a low voice:

'You read it all?'

The same white-clad senior sister answers calmly:

'I also changed three rhyme schemes; the third line is the best.'

An extreme close-up captures the junior sister's ears turning noticeably red.

The senior sister remains dignified, calm, and without any hint of mockery.

At this moment, a drop of rain from the eaves naturally falls into the same canal, making a slight and clear water sound, as the final deadpan beat.

Strictly ends at 15.0 seconds.

Cinematic realistic texture. 3. Character Lock
Character ID A | White-clad Sword Immortal: Same 25–30 year old East Asian female sword immortal. Strictly maintain: @Image 1 (same face), black long hair, slender body proportions, white embroidered silk Hanfu, jade accessories, white cloth boots, and a unique long silver sword.
Character ID B | Green-clad Rival: Same 20–25 year old East Asian female rival. Strictly maintain: @Image 2 (same face), black braided hair, petite body proportions, green Hanfu, dark cloth boots, and a unique dark steel sword.

4. Storyboard Design
Shot 1 | 0–5s | Wide or Extreme Wide Shot
Goal: Establish a misleading spatial relationship, making the audience and characters believe there is a bottomless canyon ahead.
Content: Two characters stand fully from head to toe on two ancient stone platforms covered in wet moss. Heavy mist blocks the view between them, making it look like a bottomless chasm.
Anchors: Waterfall disappears into the mist; pine branches sway naturally at different depths; water droplets flow slowly on stone; distant tiled buildings appear and disappear in the mist; rising sun pushes the mist horizontally.
Performance: Both remain cautious and restrained, as if facing a great enemy. Establish the spatial misdirection first.

Shot 2 | 5–10s | Medium or Cowboy Shot
Goal: Both misjudge the spatial scale and prepare high-consumption sword-crossing moves.
Continuity: Maintain same characters, outfits, swords, geography, mist/platform logic, and environment anchors (pines, waterfall, tiled buildings).
Action: Both enter a charging state. Wide sleeves are lifted by airflow; sword blades emit low-frequency resonance; mist swirls around ankles. Dignified, formal, and restrained posture.
Dialogue: White-clad immortal says calmly: 'This sword strike crosses the canyon.' Green-clad woman replies: 'I'll be waiting.'
Camera: Slow orbital shot around the duo. Anchors must remain visible to verify space.

Shot 3 | 10–15s | Close-up or Extreme Close-up
Goal: Complete the reversal through visibility changes. The truth must come from clearing the existing environment, not generating a new one.
Event: A natural mountain wind clears the last layer of mist. Reveal: The 'bottomless canyon' is actually just a three-step-wide ancient mountain irrigation canal. Dark water and vertical stone reflections caused the depth illusion.
Hard Constraints: Continuity of stone edges, waterfall entry, moss, pines, tiled buildings, sun direction, and mist logic. Nothing should morph suddenly.
Performance: Both freeze with swords raised. Green-clad woman looks down slowly and says: 'Maybe... just walk over?' White-clad immortal silently sheathes her sword, steps across on three existing rocks, and says impassively as she passes: 'Saves spiritual power.'
Ending: Extreme close-up of the green-clad woman trying to suppress a smile. The formerly grand 'canyon waterfall sound' now sounds like a small bubbling canal.

5. Audio-Visual & Physical Requirements
Native synchronous Mandarin dialogue; consistent spatial sound; unified physical logic for wind, mist, water, and reflections; continuous natural motion and parallax; realistic movement for silk, hair, and droplets.

6. Technical Specifications
Strict duration: 15 seconds; 16:9 aspect ratio; 3 continuous clear shots; only 2 visible characters; no subtitles.

[Reference / Character Consistency] image1 is the face/identity reference, the standard for facial and character identity. Maintain the same person across all cuts, featuring the same slender chin, blue eyes (shape and iris color), long moon-silver hair, bangs, blue rose and butterfly hair ornaments, and their fixed placement. image2 is the outfit/full-body reference. Fixed elements include a black high-neck top, black lace sleeves, deep navy short cape, blue jewel brooch, fine gold and silver decorations, navy pleated midi skirt, black lace-up boots, moon-patterned bag, and a slender silhouette. The bag is snug against the right hip. Priority if references conflict: image1 for face, eyes, and hair; image2 for everything below the neck (outfit, decorations, body type). Final facial expression sequence: eyes soften -> brows lower slightly -> eyelids narrow once -> mouth stays closed -> gaze returns forward. Only expressions, gaze, breathing, combat stances, and natural hair/fabric movement are allowed. No character changes, facial averaging, outfit swaps, horizontal flips, clones, or additional protagonists. [Equipment Consistency] Owner / ownership count: The protagonist alone carries one slender blue-silver single-edged sword; the Skeleton King alone carries one black iron greatsword. Total swords in the video are fixed at two. One dark navy scabbard is belted to the protagonist's left hip. At the start, the sword is drawn in the right hand, the scabbard is empty, and the left hand is free. No duplication or swapping of weapons, hilts, guards, or scabbards. [Enemy Consistency] Exactly three generic skeletons. As skeleton/undead, they have skulls, exposed ribs, spine, pelvis, long phalanges, blue orbital light, and torn black cloth. They have no weapons and lunge simultaneously. Exactly one Skeleton King. As skeleton/undead, he has a skull and ribs twice as large, a black iron crown fixed to the skull, thick black iron armor, a torn dark navy cloak, intense blue orbital flames, and a black iron greatsword. No shield. He appears only after the three generic soldiers are defeated. All enemies maintain solid bone, cloth, and iron materials until defeat; do not replace them with crystals or light figures. No mixing of generic and King features, and no duplication of enemies. [Rendering Consistency] Use only 3D toon/cel-look. Centered on image1 and image2, featuring thin blue-gray outlines, two-to-three layers of toon shading with soft gradients, clear moon-silver, deep navy, and royal blue. Sharp fine highlights on silver hair, with high-density material expression distinguishing velvet, lace, metal, gemstones, and glass. Character-first/character-specific palette: Prioritize the protagonist's royal blue as the character-specific key light and deep navy as the character-specific shadow. Background uses a low-saturation palette, with cyan used only as auxiliary for contact light. High density includes exterior ribs, window frames, seats, hand straps, railings, connection doors, and floor reflections. No thick outlines. No single-layer flat cel painting. No generic 3D anime faces. No smooth plastic CG materials. No low-density backgrounds. No live-action or semi-realistic styles. No dull colors. Do not mix art styles. [Common Axis of Motion and Cinematography] Combat follows one continuous trajectory. The same line of motion is passed through the rooftop advance, falling into the window, breaking into the car, being pushed outward by the King's greatsword, pivoting inward, passing behind, the return slash, and the sheathing. The trajectory deforms upon contact but does not stop to reset. Camera systems switch based on purpose: low rear-three-quarter attacker tracking, diagonal exterior view, over-the-shoulder counter, short orbit/axis change, diagonal impact push-in, and side medium close-up. Low angle heights: 0.4m for roof/floor action, 1.2m for over-the-shoulder, 1.35m for sheathing. Allow brief foreground occlusion by seats or window frames; parts of the body may exit the frame during speed sequences. The background vanishing axis always flows toward the front of the train. Cut transitions are linked by foot grounding, window impacts, weapon contact, and the direction of body passage. [Speed and Sound] Full-body movements are real-time. Hit-stop on contact is maximum 1 frame. No long charging times, slow motion, mid-air freezing, or repetitive poses. Tense strings and low percussion around 150 BPM. Synchronize visible events with footsteps on metal roof, wind pressure, glass shattering, dry bone thuds on the floor, sword collisions, armor cracking, and the final sheathing sound. No dialogue, subtitles, logos, UI, or watermarks. Cut 1: 0.0–2.0s | Sprinting on the roof Low 3/4 rear view. Roof ribs and the canyon recede at high speed; hair and cape flow sharply backward. Using the reaction force of the fourth step, she jumps from the right edge of the roof to the side of the car. At 2.0s, her head, shoulders, waist, and both legs are all outside the intact window glass; no part of her body has entered the window frame yet. Leaving the broken window behind her, the waist, knees, and boots pass through the frame by 3.7s. At 4.2s, her entire body is inside, landing low on the aisle floor. Her waist and ribcage cross one floor seam; by 6.0s, she steps between the edge of the left seat and the first skeletal arm. As the long phalanges of the front-left skeleton cross the lens, use that arm as a natural occlusion to switch to the next viewpoint. The background vanishing axis shifts from the front door to the diagonal row of windows on the back left. She catches the floor with her right sole, briefly compresses her knee, and passes her pelvis over the right foot into a low clockwise pivot. The entire sword draws a single arc at waist height; by 7.2s, her body passes through the center of the triangle formed by the three enemies. The camera does not rotate faster than the sword, showing the kick of the supporting leg and the passage of the blade simultaneously. Cut 5: 7.2–8.5s | Crossing the axis in the direction of the blade, leaving the collapse behind Triggered by the blade crossing from right to left, the camera briefly orbits from behind the right shoulder to a low left-front diagonal, dropping height from 0.8m to 0.45m and pulling back from knee-up to full body. The background vanishing axis returns from the diagonal windows to the front door. The three do not wait their turn; they simultaneously begin collapsing into bone piles behind her passage line. By 8.0s, she is completely out of the encirclement; by 8.5s, she crosses two more floor seams. She does not look back, handing the moment of her next right-foot grounding to the King's appearance. Cut 6: 8.5–11.5s | Linking the King's appearance directly to a descending arc The pressure of a black iron greatsword pushes open the connecting door, and the Skeleton King enters the aisle in one step. Without pausing the appearance pose, he carries that step directly into a vertical descending arc with the entire greatsword. The protagonist, maintaining forward momentum, brings her sword up in front of her body. At 11.5s, they enter the contact line with a clear gap remaining between the two blades, passing the speed of the descending arc to the next cut. Cut 7: 11.5–14.2s | Receiving downward pressure for an instant, then immediate disengagement From behind her left shoulder at 1.2m height, capture both weapons, the pre-contact gap, and her supporting leg in the same frame. At 11.5s, the King's greatsword is descending, with a clear gap between blades. Maintaining forward momentum, she moves her right foot to the next floor panel and aligns the hilt area of her sword with the descending line. At 14.1s, the base of the greatsword and the hilt area of the single-edged sword hit at a single point. Place a hit-stop of max 1 frame only at the moment of contact, with bluish-white sparks scattering from the impact. From the next frame, reaction force passes through her wrist, elbow, shoulder, ribcage, waist, and right foot as she kicks off the floor. At 14.2s, the blades are already moving apart; do not hold the crossed contact pose, passing the disengagement to the next cut. Cut 8: 14.2–16.0s | Passing through the inside, swapping positions within 1.8s With a short orbital wrap around the contact point, the camera moves to her right side at 0.75m height, showing both full bodies, both weapons, and floor seams. While sparks are still falling at 14.2s, her waist and ribcage move clockwise, and her sword moves away from the greatsword. The King's greatsword continues through its descending line. At 14.6s, the blades are more than one blade-width apart; her right shoulder and waist pass inside the greatsword. At 15.2s, she is completely past the King, and her waist crosses the next floor seam. By 15.5s, their front/back positions are fully swapped. The King is not left behind, tracking her with his upper body and greatsword. At 15.8s, he converts the remaining body rotation from the descending arc into a horizontal return arc. At 16.0s, the greatsword has already begun horizontal movement; she is half-way through a step toward the outside of the aisle, continuing the motion into the next cut. Cut 9: 16.0–18.5s | Carrying the return arc into the next contact The camera recedes along the attack line from a front-right diagonal at 1.0m height, capturing the King's full body, the greatsword, and her supporting leg. From 16.0s, the King continues swinging the greatsword in a horizontal arc; by 16.8s, the tip crosses the aisle center line. She does not retreat, placing her left foot half-way onto another floor panel outside the aisle and bringing the middle of her blade into the path of the greatsword. The King returns reaction force from the floor through his soles, moving shoulders and waist in the same direction as the horizontal arc. She matches that force with her blade, carrying that momentum until just before the next attack contact. At 17.6s, both waist positions cross different floor seams, with a gap still between blades. At 18.5s, pass the non-static moment where the return arc and parry trajectory are nearly touching to the next cut. Cut 10: 18.5–26.8s | Resolving from the return contact with the same rotation Low diagonal view with seats in the foreground. At 18.5s, there is still a finger-width gap between blades. At 18.8s, the middle of the greatsword and the middle of her sword hit. Hit-stop is max 1 frame. At 18.9s, blades separate, her supporting leg converts lateral pressure into forward speed, and she passes the King. The clockwise rotation remaining from the passage closes into a single sword trajectory returning diagonally upward, crossing the front of the undamaged black iron armor. Only after that passage do thin blue cracks run through the armor and the orbital flames extinguish. The King collapses to the floor in the order of legs, torso, and greatsword; the greatsword stops lying flat. She takes two steps in the same direction and half-turns with the fallen King behind her. Cut 11: 26.8–30.0s | Finalizing with sword sheathing Close-up side-diagonal view capturing face, hands, and the scabbard mouth at the left hip. Left hand supports the scabbard, right hand rotates the sword to align the tip with the actual scabbard mouth. After the tip enters, the blade is sheathed continuously to the end. At 29.7s, the guard meets the scabbard mouth, synchronized with a dry metallic 'click' sound. The bones of the three skeletons, the fallen King, and the horizontal greatsword are static in the background. Simultaneously with the 29.7s sheathing, perform the short facial expression change mentioned above. At 30.0s, cut the scene in the finalized state just before the right hand leaves the hilt.

prompt: High-quality anime footage. Near-future Gothic fantasy. Cinematic theatrical anime battle footage. High-density 3D Toon/Cel look only. Maintain theatrical-class key animation, high-quality compositing, smooth continuous motion with readable center of gravity, transparent lighting, and high-density background art. [Animation Direction] Explosive and sharp action. Sharp timing. Minimal anticipatory movements. Instant acceleration. Large, clear full-body movements. Strong contact recoil. Clearly leave inertia after contact. Dynamic camera integrated with movement. High kinetic energy. No waiting, long stances, long charging, slow recovery, or slow motion. [Role and Priority of References] <<<Image1>>> is the highest priority reference for face and character identity. Refer to facial features, age, eyes, iris, eyelashes, cheeks, jaw, bangs, horns, and drawings around the face. <<<Image2>>> is for costume, full-body design, and weapon reference. Refer to the same person's costume, decorations, body type, full-body silhouette, shoes, single long spear, and specific color scheme as in <<<Image1>>>. 3 is for tail reference. Refer to the connection position to the back of the waist, obsidian purple scales, a single tail naturally tapering from the base to the thin tip, and the purple light at the tip of the tail, same as the person in <<<Image1>>> and <<<Image2>>>. If there are differences between references, prioritize <<<Image1>>> for face, eyes, iris, jaw, age, bangs, and horns; <<<Image2>>> for costume, decorations, body type, and long spear; and <<<Image3>>> for tail connection position, scales, thickness, and tip shape. Do not copy backgrounds, text, frames, multiple panels, explanatory diagrams, or UI from reference images into the footage. [Fixed Protagonist] The protagonist is the same single dragon girl throughout. Maintain <<<Image1>>>'s small, delicate oval face, thin jaw, pale skin, small nose and mouth, large purple to amethyst eyes with multi-layered sparkle, delicate upper eyelashes, dark purple-black short bob with blue-purple highlights at the ends, and two curved black-purple horns on both sides in all cuts. Maintain <<<Image2>>>'s slender and well-proportioned body, black to deep purple high-collared Gothic costume, white chest cloth, thin gold edges and chain decorations, purple-black cape and wide sleeves, dark tights, black shoes, and single long spear. Maintain <<<Image3>>>'s single organic scaled tail connected continuously to the back of the waist, from obsidian purple scales to the thin glowing tip. Do not de-identify or simplify even in distant views or high-speed movements. In close-ups, return to the eye spacing, iris pattern, thin jaw, bangs, and horn positions of <<<Image1>>>. Maintain the same face, hair, horns, costume, body type, spear, tail, and color scheme; only facial expressions, gaze, breathing, combat stance, and natural delay of hair/cloth/tail may change. [Fixed Enemy] The enemy is a single, giant organic Yokai-Oni. Approximately twice the size of the protagonist, with soot-colored dark gray-purple rough skin, two ivory-colored horns extending backward, dark red glowing eyes, an ogre face with fangs, long messy black hair, a torn black-purple haori, and a single dark red glowing curse mark in the center of the front. Maintain the same design in all cuts; do not change into crystalline or crystal statues. Do not mix the face, eyes, hair, horns, costume, physique, or color scheme of the protagonist and the Oni. Avoid face averaging, costume swapping, cloning, or extra characters. [Shared Art Style] Line art is thin and delicate, line color is dark blue to blue-purple. Clear two-to-three-stage cel shading and pale intermediate shadows on face, hair, costume, horns, tail, and Oni. Shadows are centered on blue-purple and dark blue, not crushed to black. During movement, cel shadow boundaries should follow the 3D volume, with no flickering or irrelevant flipping. Color scheme is black, deep purple, amethyst, subtle gold, and soft white. Eyes and tail tip have multi-layered purple light, hair has thin blue-purple silk-like highlights, and skin is a clean matte anime style. Place incandescent areas only in narrow ranges at the center of contact, leaving high-saturation amethyst and black-purple around them to prevent whiteout. Distinguish cloth, metal, horns, scales, and glass with different reflections. Use directional motion blur only for high-speed parts; faces, eyes, hands, spearheads, and butts must be clearly readable. Soft cool white key light + weak warm fill on the protagonist's face. Background is low-saturation blue-gray and white-gray. Do not use thick black outlines, simplified TV anime style, flat coloring, generic 3D bishoujo faces, plastic CG, semi-realistic, realistic, live-action, or mixed art styles. [Temporal Continuity & Physics] Move stride, breathing, and tail sway from the start of the footage; no explanatory stills. The beginning of each cut inherits the end pose, speed, rotation direction, and screen progression direction of the previous cut; no re-posing, standing idle, or teleporting to starting positions. Supporting legs are fixed to the floor; do not slide soles at stepping, landing, or rotation pivots. Landing is sole contact -> knee compression -> waist sinking -> upper body follow-through. Spear reaction force is not absorbed by wrists alone; flow from elbow -> shoulder -> waist -> supporting leg to the next movement. Hair, sleeves, chains, capes, chest cloths, and tails are not integrated; they have different delays in the order of body -> hair/sleeves -> chains/cape -> tail tip. Hands maintain positions on the shaft; regripping is one hand at a time. Do not fuse fingers, wrists, and shaft; maintain front-back relationships of horns, hair, arms, spear, and tail. [Stage & Lighting] A near-future combat atrium with a giant glass ceiling and a two-level corridor. Thick white-gray structural beams, reinforced glass showing a pale blue sky, deep corridors, low-saturation mechanical equipment, and a polished light-gray reinforced glass floor. The floor softly reflects the girl, Oni, spear, and purple light. Clear parallax with three levels of depth: foreground beams, middle corridors, and distant glass walls. After falling, maintain the beam direction, light source, and vertical relationship of openings as the lower level of the same building. No readable characters, signs, advertisements, or logos. Uniform the direction of the cool white key light in all cuts. Blue-purple rim on the girl, Oni's dark red light reflects on the Oni and surrounding floor, and the girl's amethyst light reflects only on the girl, spear, tail, and nearby glass. No sudden exposure changes after large flashes. Do not hide faces, hands, spear structure, or Oni's curse mark with smoke or bloom. Use camera shake briefly only for strong contact and floor breakage. [Weapon & Tail] Only one long spear. Only the girl is the owner. Black long shaft, subtle gold decorations, one amethyst glowing spearhead, and one butt. Spearhead, shaft, and butt are always connected in a single straight line, maintaining the same total length, thickness, and decoration positions. No shrinking, bending, duplication, or deformation. Hands release only during throwing; order: empty hands -> same single spear in flight -> return -> grabbing the same shaft with both hands. During rotation, the entire spear revolves largely around the body as a single rigid body. Do not rotate only the spearhead; no transformation into propellers, windmills, or multiple blades. Only one tail. Continuously connected from the back of the waist; force is transmitted in the order of waist rotation -> base -> middle -> tail tip. No branching, duplication, or transformation into another creature. [Contact Causality] All contact must strictly follow the sequence: trajectory/gap/undamaged state before contact -> contact at specified position -> local light/crack/cloth displacement/gravity shift after contact. Do not generate magic waves, crystals, sparks, or glass cracks before contact. [Cut 1 | Approach] Rear diagonal mid-distant view near the floor. Start from the girl's back, camera moves forward as if catching up with the girl toward the Oni at the end of the corridor. The girl steps deep while keeping a single spear tilted diagonally backward and swaying a single tail low. Weight shift from heel -> sole -> toe. Cape and tail delay by half a beat. Shift axis over the Oni's shoulder, spear shaft crosses in front of the lens in foreground occlusion to a short close-up of the same face as <<<Image1>>>. Purple eyes catch the Oni, eyebrows slightly down, upper eyelids narrowed, mouth closed. Sink supporting leg and pass that momentum to the next rotation. Do not show the face static. [Cut 2 | Barrier Contact and Full Spear Rotation] Oni blocks the path with a dark red curse barrier. The girl doesn't stop, coordinates waist, shoulders, and hands to swing the single long spear largely around the body, continuous sweep from low diagonal to high diagonal. Hair, cape, and tail delay by half a beat. Camera moves diagonally around the outside of the shaft from waist-high mid-view, showing supporting leg, hands, full spear length, and contact point in the same motion. Thin gap between spear and barrier before contact. Short hit-stop only at the moment of contact. Thin amethyst circular wave is born only after contact, Oni's haori and messy hair flow backward. Connect reaction force to the next release. [Cut 3 | Throw, Return, Catch, Jump] Girl releases the shaft at the furthest point of rotation. Only the same single spear maintains a straight line, pulling a thin amethyst trajectory and flying toward the barrier. Oni tilts the barrier to parry, changing the spear's trajectory into a large return arc. Briefly show empty hands and the single spear in flight; girl grabs near the center of the returned shaft with both hands. Catch inertia transmits to upper body -> center of gravity. Kick the floor with that reaction force and jump over the Oni. Low close-up camera also rises along the spear's arc, changing from mid-view to full-body diagonal top view. Show throwing -> same spear return -> regrabbing -> rising in one sequence. Align spear with body centerline in mid-air, then turn to descent. [Cut 4 | Descent Contact, Crystal, Landing Rotation, Kick] Space between Oni's curse mark and spear tip before descent. Short hit-stop and narrow incandescent core only at the moment the spearhead contacts the curse mark. Only after contact, giant crystal ridges of obsidian purple -> high-saturation amethyst -> pale lavender rise in a fan shape. Crystals have three layers: thick main ridges, branching thin sub-ridges, and fine fragments. Translucent magic crystals of the protagonist's unique color, not bluish ice. Oni itself does not crystallize. Girl changes reaction force into a landing rotation, swinging the entire spear once diagonally. High mid-view camera also moves around the crystal in the foreground to the opposite side, flipping the axis from ceiling direction to floor direction. Briefly ground the same spearhead on the empty floor away from the Oni, rotate the body at a low center of gravity using the single spear as a pivot, and kick the Oni away.
